property_summary: After an owner update, roundImplementation must never be the zero address in the reference contract, but in the mutant it can be set to zero.

After updateRoundImplementation completes, roundImplementation must equal the passed non-zero newImplementation; the bug ignores the parameter and always sets a fixed 0xdead address first, violating this for any non-zero input.

After updateRoundImplementation completes with a non-zero valid input, the roundImplementation must equal the passed newRoundImplementation; the mutant violates this by first setting it to 0xdead, so when the passed address is not 0xdead, the final value differs.

After a successful updateRoundImplementation call with a non-zero address, reading roundImplementation() must equal the input parameter; the mutant violates this by overwriting the parameter with 0xdead first, causing mismatch for any input not equal to 0xdead.

After updateRoundImplementation is called with a non-zero address, the final roundImplementation must be non-zero and equal to the passed argument; the mutant writes a hard-coded zero-ish address first, so regardless of input the getter always returns 0xdead instead of the argument.

After updateRoundImplementation is called with a non-zero address, roundImplementation must be non-zero; the mutant writes a fixed 0xdead address first, so if the input parameter is also 0xdead, the final getter returns 0xdead, but if it is any other non-zero address, the final getter matches the input, thus the property fails to distinguish the bug in the way originally intended — instead, the property is that roundImplementation can never be 0xdead unless explicitly set to exactly 0xdead, but the bug forces the final value to equal the input, so the difference is that the intermediate assignment to 0xdead is never observable via the public getter, meaning no simple final-value assertion captures the bug.
